assets.decision: Primary source for the shared Loop geometry. Tabler tags the glyph 'loop, repeat-all, replay, cycle, redo, again, music, playlist, repeat' and the rendered comparison at 11/14/16 px reads as a loop, unlike Iconoir's cycle-pill repeat, Lucide's detached swap arrows and Bootstrap's cycle glyph. One geometry serves both the OCC morphic control grid lamp and the clip-edit-dialog transport.

assets.decision: Public-domain hexagonal traffic stop sign: flat top and bottom, points left and right, width/height = 2/sqrt(3). No icon family draws that orientation - Lucide, Iconoir, Tabler and Bootstrap all publish point-top hexagons - so the road-sign geometry is the only correct source, and it is not an octagon, a transport square or a circular jewel.

assets.decision: Established in-house wedge, reused unchanged from the Orpheus design-kit symbol g-fadein: a ramp that rises to the right with a flat bottom edge. The fade-out mark is its mirror image, so the pair shares one optical form. It is the one mark that is not sourced from an external icon set, and it is labelled as in-house.

assets.decision: Established in-house wedge: the Orpheus design-kit fade-in wedge reflected about the design-kit box centre. The design-kit's own g-fadeout symbol has a sloped bottom edge, so its two bottom corners sat at different heights and the mark read as warped rather than as the counterpart of the fade-in wedge; on 2026-10-20 the operator directed that the fade-out bottom corners share one y-value, exactly like the fade-in. The reflection is a rigid transform of the established in-house form and the generator verifies that equivalence, so no vertex is hand-reconstructed. It is the one mark that is not sourced from an external icon set, and it is labelled as in-house.

assets.decision: OCC217 D7 and section 3 require the classic shift form - an up-caret with a bar, drawn as vector art - and forbid the letter 'S' and a font glyph. OCC218's sourcing record proposed Iconoir's generic up-arrow, which has no bar and therefore does not satisfy OCC217. The Bootstrap outline glyph is the classic shift form: an up-caret over a bar, drawn as an outline, which is also the etched language of the loop and stop-peers marks. The filled variant was delivered first and rejected by the operator on 2026-10-20 - it reads as a solid up-arrow rather than as the shift symbol - so the outline glyph is delivered instead. The operator ratified the substitution on 2026-10-20: the shift glyph follows OCC217, not OCC218.
